lastCompletedStory.title: Planner rule: a hand-file-via-/cam-issue requirement is an on-main oracle, never a worker story

nextStoryContext: Both subagent-planner.md copies (.claude/agents/ and templates/agents/) now carry a new rule paragraph immediately after the pre-existing `requires:'operator'` paragraph: a 'hand-file issue via /cam-issue' requirement must NEVER be emitted as a worker implementation story (writing scripts/cam/issues/CAM-XXXX.json on-branch causes an add/add collision when the branch reconciles with main -- the CAM-162 defect). It must instead be encoded as a file-assert oracle acceptance criterion verifying the issue exists on main, e.g. `[oracle: file-assert git show main:scripts/cam/issues/CAM-XXXX.json]`. Both subagent-reviewer.md copies gained one clarifying line (right after the existing 'artifact-of-record is the reviewer's Layer B evidence' sentence) confirming this on-main existence check is a legitimate file-assert oracle target for the reviewer's existing Layer B re-run -- no new reviewer gate code was added. src/vendor/_generated.ts was regenerated (bun run embed-vendor) and embed-vendor:check is clean. This is prompt-only guidance with no new unit test (per the story's notes: an LLM-prompt-output assertion would be brittle; the US-001 hook is the real enforcement mechanism for the sibling worker-actor deny-set, this story is purely a planner-authoring-time rule). If a future story needs another 'X is never a worker story, it's an on-main oracle' rule (e.g. for other control-plane actions), append it to the SAME paragraph block in both subagent-planner.md copies, next to the requires:'operator' and hand-file rules, keeping the dual-copy-per-file wording style (CAM-123 precedent: cam-specific vs. generic phrasing, same principle).
